Spectral¶

Implemented in backend/app/routers/spectral.py. All endpoints require X-Visivo-Token and, except /v1/spectral/linefit, X-Visivo-Session. Line-width maps, baseline subtraction, spectral stacking, spectrum extraction, line fitting and source finding.

Line width, baseline and stacking¶

POST /v1/spectral/linewidth¶

Per-pixel line-width map. Returns both FWHM (Gaussian fit) and equivalent-width maps as base64 float32.

{
  "dataset_id": "...",
  "channel_start": 10,
  "channel_end": 50,
  "mask_enabled": false,
  "threshold_value": 0.0,
  "method": null,
  "rest_freq_hz": null
}

method: null = both maps (JSON path); "fwhm" or "ew" selects one (binary path). rest_freq_hz: rest frequency in Hz for velocity-axis conversion (FWHM only).

Response: valid, width, height, scalar_type, fwhm_unit, ew_unit, bunit, fwhm_range_min/max, ew_range_min/max, fwhm_base64, ew_base64.

POST /v1/spectral/linewidth/binary¶

Same request. Returns a binary payload: with method "fwhm" or "ew" one frame, otherwise two concatenated frames (FWHM then EW). Each frame is a 12-byte big-endian header of three uint32 values (rows, columns, flags = 0) followed by little-endian float32 pixels in row-major order, NaN for masked pixels. Use BackendClient::parseBinaryFrame() to decode.

GET /v1/spectral/linewidth/{dataset_id}¶

Retrieve a previously computed linewidth result by dataset ID.

POST /v1/spectral/baseline/{session_id}/{dataset_id}¶

Fit and subtract a per-pixel polynomial or median baseline from a spectral cube.

{
  "session_id": "...",
  "dataset_id": "...",
  "channel_start": 0,
  "channel_end": 0,
  "poly_order": 1,
  "method": "polynomial",
  "line_free_channels": [[5, 15], [80, 120]]
}

method: "polynomial" or "median". line_free_channels: flat list [5, 6, 7] or list of ranges [[5, 15], [80, 120]].

Response: valid, new_dataset_id (registered in session — use it directly for moment computation), width, height, depth, range_min/max, poly_order, method, fit_channels, rms_before, rms_after, output_path.

POST /v1/spectral/stack¶

Stack N open cubes into a single combined spectrum map.

{
  "dataset_ids": ["...", "..."],
  "method": "mean",
  "weight_by": "uniform",
  "weights": []
}

method: "mean" (default), "median", "weighted_mean". weight_by: "uniform", "rms", "peak" (used when method="weighted_mean" and weights is empty). weights: explicit per-cube weights (used only for "weighted_mean").

Response: valid, rows, cols, scalar_type, method, n_cubes, range_min/max, data_base64.

POST /v1/spectral/stack/binary¶

Same request. Returns a single binary frame (same format as /linewidth/binary).

Profiles and line fitting¶

Spectra are extracted on the node, so the profiler works on multi-GB remote cubes. The spectral axis is the cube’s third axis, converted to world values through the WCS when it has a spectral axis, otherwise channel numbers with spectral_unit: "pix" and spectral_type: "CHANNEL". Non-finite values come back as null.

POST /v1/spectral/probe¶

The spectrum at one pixel.

{ "dataset_id": "...", "x": 120.0, "y": 88.0 }

x, y are 0-based pixels, rounded to the nearest integer. Response: valid, error, x, y, spectral_axis, spectral_unit, spectral_type, values. A pixel outside the image, or a dataset that is not a 3-D cube, is 400; a non-cube dataset entry is 422.

POST /v1/spectral/aperture¶

The mean spectrum over a circular aperture (NaN-aware mean per channel).

{ "dataset_id": "...", "x": 120.0, "y": 88.0, "radius": 3.0 }

radius is in pixels (default 3). Response: valid, error, x, y, radius, n_pix, spectral_axis, spectral_unit, spectral_type, values. An aperture that covers no pixel is 400.

POST /v1/spectral/linefit¶

Fit one Gaussian, plus an optional linear baseline, to a spectrum the caller supplies. Stateless: no dataset or session is involved, so the same fit serves probes, aperture spectra and any external profile.

{ "values": [0.01, 0.02, 0.35, 0.81, 0.33, 0.03],
  "axis":   [1500, 1510, 1520, 1530, 1540, 1550],
  "with_baseline": true }

At least 4 finite samples are needed; values and axis of different length, or a fit that does not converge, is 422. Response, in the axis units: peak, center, sigma, fwhm, integrated_flux (amp·σ·√(2π)), each with an _err companion (null when undefined), continuum (baseline at the line centre), equivalent_width (null without a baseline or with zero continuum), baseline ([a, b] of a + b·x), rms of the residuals, n_points, spectral_correlation_factor and spectral_correlation_note. The errors are inflated by the measured residual autocorrelation factor (1.0 for independent channels); the note is non-empty when the factor is 2.25 or more, warning that the cause may be a poor model rather than correlated channels.

Source finding (synchronous)¶

POST /v1/sourcefind/{dataset_id}¶

Run SoFiA-2 on a cube and wait for the result. Body: {sofia_params} (SoFiA parameters as a dictionary; a dataset_id field is accepted and ignored, the path parameter is used).

Response: valid, error, n_sources, sources, mask_path, catalog_path (empty when SoFiA did not write them). A non-cube dataset is 422; no SoFiA-2 executable is 503; a SoFiA failure is valid: false with the message. A run is limited to VISIVO_SOFIA_TIMEOUT_S (default 900 s). The task-based route /v1/tasks/sourcefind can be polled and cancelled and also offers the photutils finder.
